title: [ARCH-11] Rigorous CI, Immutable Containers and Release Artifacts
body:
## Architecture implementation ticket

This architecture ticket is binding across the StrataAI2 functional PRDs.

### Adopted StrataAI2 CI architecture

StrataAI2 uses a **rigorous build-once / test-the-artifact / promote-the-same-artifact** CI model.

The pipeline must build exactly three application images from the tested commit:

- `strataai-web`
- `strataai-api`
- `strataai-worker`

The exact image artifacts that pass integration, E2E, security and smoke testing are the artifacts exported in the downloadable release bundle and, on approved branches/tags, published to GHCR. **No downstream release or publish job may rebuild application source.**

The expected pipeline is:

```text
PR / push / release tag
        |
        v
 metadata + changed commit identity
        |
        +------------------+-------------------+
        |                  |                   |
        v                  v                   v
   web-quality       dotnet-quality     postgres-integration
        |                  |                   |
        +------------------+-------------------+
                           |
                           v
                    source-quality-gate
                           |
                           v
                    build-images-once
                           |
              +------------+------------+
              |            |            |
              v            v            v
        web image      api image     worker image
              \            |            /
               +-----------+------------+
                           |
                immutable image artifacts
                           |
          +----------------+----------------+
          |                |                |
          v                v                v
 container-integration    e2e          security/supply-chain
          |                |                |
          +----------------+----------------+
                           |
                           v
                     required-ci
                           |
                  +--------+--------+
                  |                 |
                  v                 v
             release-bundle     publish-images
             (PR/main/tag)      (main/tag only)
```

---

# ARCH-11 — Rigorous CI, Immutable Containers and Release Artifacts

## 1. PRD identifier
**ARCH-11**

## 2. Feature name
**Rigorous CI, Immutable Containers and Release Artifacts**

## 3. Executive summary

Implement a GitHub Actions CI pipeline that validates source quality, exercises the real PostgreSQL/pgvector security boundary, builds web/API/Worker containers exactly once, runs integration and browser tests against those exact images, performs software-supply-chain checks, and emits the tested images as a Docker-loadable release bundle.

A successful CI run is therefore evidence not merely that the source compiled, but that the **actual deployable StrataAI2 container artifacts** passed the required quality, security and runtime checks.

## 4. Problem statement

A pipeline that only runs unit tests or builds ephemeral containers is insufficient for StrataAI2.

The application has cross-cutting risks that only appear in realistic runtime conditions, including:

- Organization/tenant isolation and PostgreSQL RLS;
- database migration failures;
- pgvector extension/retrieval behaviour;
- Owner Portal versus internal authorization boundaries;
- Worker/outbox job behaviour;
- duplicate/replayed background work;
- SignalR/realtime behaviour;
- object-storage access;
- web-to-API reverse proxying;
- container startup and health;
- supply-chain vulnerabilities;
- divergence between the image tested in CI and the image later released.

The CI architecture must therefore prove the deployable system, not merely the source tree.

## 5. Product objective

Provide a deterministic, security-conscious, traceable CI pipeline where:

1. every required test gate is automated;
2. the deployable web/API/Worker images are built exactly once;
3. downstream jobs test the exact built image artifacts;
4. failed mandatory checks prevent release artifacts;
5. a successful CI artifact can run on a clean Docker host without rebuilding source;
6. release provenance can be traced to one exact Git commit and workflow run.

## 6. User personas

- Software developer
- Coding/build agent
- Technical architect
- DevOps/release engineer
- Security/privacy reviewer
- System administrator
- Quality engineer

## 7. User stories

- As a developer, I receive fast feedback on TypeScript, .NET, database and integration regressions.
- As a coding agent, I have one explicit CI contract defining what must pass before an issue can be considered complete.
- As a security reviewer, I can verify tenant isolation, dependency scanning, secret detection, SBOMs and artifact provenance.
- As a release engineer, I can deploy the exact Docker images that CI tested.
- As an operator, I can download a release bundle and start StrataAI2 without cloning source or installing Node/.NET.
- As a maintainer, I have one stable required status that can be used for branch protection even if internal CI jobs evolve.

## 8. Functional requirements

### Workflow triggers and execution safety

- **ARCH-11-FR-001** — CI SHALL run for pull requests targeting the default branch and pushes to the default branch.
- **ARCH-11-FR-002** — CI SHALL run for version/release tags used to create releasable builds.
- **ARCH-11-FR-003** — CI SHOULD support manual `workflow_dispatch` for diagnostics/rebuild of the same source ref where permitted.
- **ARCH-11-FR-004** — CI SHALL use workflow concurrency so superseded PR runs are cancelled, while main/tag release runs are not accidentally cancelled by unrelated commits.
- **ARCH-11-FR-005** — Untrusted pull-request code SHALL NOT receive privileged production/project/registry secrets. Privileged release/publish operations SHALL be restricted to trusted repository refs/environments.
- **ARCH-11-FR-006** — CI SHALL use the exact triggering commit SHA as the source identity. Release jobs SHALL NOT silently change refs or rebuild from a moving branch.
- **ARCH-11-FR-007** — Third-party GitHub Actions used by the required pipeline SHOULD be pinned to immutable commit SHAs, with controlled dependency-update processes.

### Source metadata

- **ARCH-11-FR-008** — An initial metadata job SHALL calculate and expose commit SHA, short SHA, semantic/release version where available, workflow run ID and image tag/version metadata.
- **ARCH-11-FR-009** — All later artifacts SHALL include source repository, commit SHA, workflow run ID and application version/build ID.
- **ARCH-11-FR-010** — Web, API and Worker SHALL expose compatible build/revision metadata at runtime for diagnostics.

### Web quality

- **ARCH-11-FR-011** — `web-quality` SHALL use the committed package lock and deterministic dependency installation such as `npm ci`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-012** — `web-quality` SHALL run TypeScript type checking.
- **ARCH-11-FR-013** — `web-quality` SHALL run ESLint with zero new warnings/errors under the configured policy.
- **ARCH-11-FR-014** — `web-quality` SHALL run Vitest/React Testing Library tests.
- **ARCH-11-FR-015** — Web tests SHALL include MUI component behaviour and accessibility-relevant interaction tests.
- **ARCH-11-FR-016** — Kanban tests SHALL cover `dnd-kit` pointer and keyboard movement semantics where Kanban functionality is present.
- **ARCH-11-FR-017** — `web-quality` SHALL produce a production Vite build.
- **ARCH-11-FR-018** — Web test/coverage results SHALL be retained in a machine-readable format suitable for CI diagnosis.

### .NET quality

- **ARCH-11-FR-019** — `dotnet-quality` SHALL restore dependencies from committed project/lock configuration where applicable.
- **ARCH-11-FR-020** — `dotnet-quality` SHALL compile Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API and Worker in Release configuration.
- **ARCH-11-FR-021** — .NET warnings SHALL be treated as errors according to the repository policy.
- **ARCH-11-FR-022** — `dotnet-quality` SHALL run xUnit unit/application tests across relevant projects.
- **ARCH-11-FR-023** — API tests SHALL include authentication, authorization, validation and stable error-contract coverage.
- **ARCH-11-FR-024** — Worker tests SHALL include job idempotency, retries, dead-letter/failure state and tenant-context propagation.

### PostgreSQL / pgvector / migration integration

- **ARCH-11-FR-025** — `postgres-integration` SHALL run against a real PostgreSQL 17+ instance with pgvector enabled rather than an in-memory/fake database.
- **ARCH-11-FR-026** — CI SHALL apply all ordered schema migrations to an empty database and verify successful startup/schema compatibility.
- **ARCH-11-FR-027** — CI SHALL test upgrade from at least the previous supported schema baseline to the current schema when such baseline exists.
- **ARCH-11-FR-028** — CI SHALL verify required foreign keys, unique/check constraints and critical indexes where practicable.
- **ARCH-11-FR-029** — CI SHALL verify PostgreSQL RLS/tenant isolation with at least two Organizations and attempted cross-tenant reads/writes.
- **ARCH-11-FR-030** — CI SHALL verify that missing/malformed tenant context fails closed.
- **ARCH-11-FR-031** — CI SHALL verify pgvector extension availability and representative semantic-vector persistence/query behaviour once vector functionality is implemented.
- **ARCH-11-FR-032** — CI SHALL verify append-only/audit protections that are enforced at the database layer.

### Source quality gate

- **ARCH-11-FR-033** — A `source-quality-gate` job SHALL depend on all required web, .NET and PostgreSQL source/integration jobs.
- **ARCH-11-FR-034** — Container images SHALL NOT be considered releasable when any mandatory source-quality dependency fails.
- **ARCH-11-FR-035** — The gate job SHALL contain explicit dependency-result validation rather than passing when an upstream required job is skipped unexpectedly.

### Build images once

- **ARCH-11-FR-036** — After the source quality gate passes, CI SHALL build exactly three application images: `strataai-web`, `strataai-api`, and `strataai-worker`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-037** — Each image SHALL be built exactly once per CI release candidate. Downstream test, scan, bundle and publish jobs SHALL consume those exact built image artifacts/digests.
- **ARCH-11-FR-038** — CI SHALL NOT rebuild source separately for publishing or release bundling.
- **ARCH-11-FR-039** — Images SHALL be tagged with immutable commit-derived tags such as `strataai-api:<sha>`, `strataai-worker:<sha>`, and `strataai-web:<sha>`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-040** — Images SHALL include OCI labels for repository URL, revision/commit SHA, build/version and build timestamp.
- **ARCH-11-FR-041** — Images SHALL be exported from the build job in a Docker-loadable/OCI-compatible artifact format that downstream jobs can load without rebuilding.
- **ARCH-11-FR-042** — Build-time credentials/secrets SHALL use secure build-secret mechanisms and SHALL NOT remain in image layers/history.
- **ARCH-11-FR-043** — The image build SHOULD use deterministic BuildKit/buildx caching keyed by dependency/lock inputs without allowing untrusted cache content to alter the final verified artifact.

### Real-container integration stack

- **ARCH-11-FR-044** — `container-integration` SHALL download/load the exact web/API/Worker image artifacts created by `build-images-once`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-045** — Integration CI SHALL boot a Compose/runtime topology containing the exact app images plus PostgreSQL+pgvector and object-storage parity where applicable (e.g. MinIO for local CI).
- **ARCH-11-FR-046** — The integration Compose definition SHALL use `image:` for app services and SHALL NOT use `build:`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-047** — CI SHALL validate database migration/startup using the containerized API/approved migration mechanism.
- **ARCH-11-FR-048** — CI SHALL verify API liveness/readiness.
- **ARCH-11-FR-049** — CI SHALL verify Worker liveness/operational readiness or an equivalent worker heartbeat/job-processing diagnostic.
- **ARCH-11-FR-050** — CI SHALL verify the web container serves the compiled SPA.
- **ARCH-11-FR-051** — CI SHALL verify web -> Nginx -> API reverse proxy health using the externally exposed web endpoint.
- **ARCH-11-FR-052** — CI SHALL verify graceful container shutdown/restart behaviour for API and Worker at least in smoke/integration coverage.
- **ARCH-11-FR-053** — Integration failures SHALL retain relevant container logs as CI artifacts.

### End-to-end tests

- **ARCH-11-FR-054** — `e2e` SHALL run against the exact containerized release candidate rather than separately launched development servers.
- **ARCH-11-FR-055** — Browser E2E SHALL use Playwright or an approved equivalent.
- **ARCH-11-FR-056** — E2E SHALL cover at minimum authenticated internal-app startup, core navigation and one representative create/read/update flow once those features exist.
- **ARCH-11-FR-057** — When implemented, E2E SHALL cover owner-portal isolation from internal Council/Management data.
- **ARCH-11-FR-058** — When implemented, E2E SHALL cover representative Kanban drag/drop persistence.
- **ARCH-11-FR-059** — When implemented, E2E/integration SHALL cover SignalR/realtime update/reconnect behaviour.
- **ARCH-11-FR-060** — When implemented, E2E/integration SHALL cover a representative Worker/outbox job progressing from persisted request through completed domain state.
- **ARCH-11-FR-061** — Failed Playwright runs SHALL retain traces/screenshots/videos according to the configured failure-artifact policy.

### Security and software supply chain

- **ARCH-11-FR-062** — CI SHALL run dependency vulnerability checks appropriate to Node and .NET.
- **ARCH-11-FR-063** — CI SHALL run secret-detection scanning against repository content/history according to the configured policy.
- **ARCH-11-FR-064** — CI SHALL scan all three exact application images for known vulnerabilities before release/publish.
- **ARCH-11-FR-065** — The blocking vulnerability policy SHALL be documented. Initial default SHOULD block newly introduced exploitable Critical vulnerabilities and SHOULD block High vulnerabilities when a fix is available, subject to an explicit audited exception process.
- **ARCH-11-FR-066** — CI SHALL generate an SBOM for web, API and Worker images in a standard machine-readable format such as SPDX or CycloneDX.
- **ARCH-11-FR-067** — CI SHOULD generate GitHub artifact attestations/SLSA-compatible provenance for release artifacts/images where repository/platform capability permits.
- **ARCH-11-FR-068** — Security scan output SHALL be retained for diagnosis and release evidence.
- **ARCH-11-FR-069** — A failed mandatory security gate SHALL prevent successful release/publish.

### Final required CI gate

- **ARCH-11-FR-070** — A stable final aggregate job/check named `required-ci` (or another deliberately stable name) SHALL depend on all mandatory source-quality, image-build, container-integration, E2E and security jobs.
- **ARCH-11-FR-071** — Branch/ruleset protection SHOULD require the stable final aggregate check rather than depending directly on every internal job name.
- **ARCH-11-FR-072** — `required-ci` SHALL fail if a mandatory dependency failed, was cancelled, or was unexpectedly skipped.
- **ARCH-11-FR-073** — Release/publish jobs SHALL depend on successful `required-ci`.

### Downloadable release bundle

- **ARCH-11-FR-074** — After `required-ci`, CI SHALL create `strataai2-docker-bundle-<sha>`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-075** — The bundle SHALL contain the exact tested web/API/Worker image archives.
- **ARCH-11-FR-076** — The bundle SHALL contain `compose.release.yml` that references the included image tags and has no app `build:` directives.
- **ARCH-11-FR-077** — The bundle SHALL contain `.env.release.example` containing placeholders/documented configuration only, never real secrets.
- **ARCH-11-FR-078** — The bundle SHALL contain `SHA256SUMS`.
- **ARCH-11-FR-079** — The bundle SHALL contain build metadata including repository, commit SHA, workflow run, image tags/digests and build version.
- **ARCH-11-FR-080** — The bundle SHALL contain SBOMs for web/API/Worker and security/provenance metadata required by policy.
- **ARCH-11-FR-081** — The bundle SHALL contain concise run instructions covering image load, environment setup, `docker compose up`, health verification and shutdown.
- **ARCH-11-FR-082** — The release bundle SHALL be usable on a clean Docker Desktop/Engine machine without Node, .NET SDK or source checkout.
- **ARCH-11-FR-083** — CI SHALL verify checksums and bundle completeness before uploading the artifact.
- **ARCH-11-FR-084** — PR artifacts SHOULD have a shorter retention period (default target: 14 days); main/tag release artifacts SHOULD have a longer retention period (default target: 90 days or repository policy).

### Registry publication

- **ARCH-11-FR-085** — On trusted default-branch and/or version-tag runs, CI MAY publish the exact already-tested images to GHCR.
- **ARCH-11-FR-086** — Registry publication SHALL use the exact artifact/digest that passed `required-ci`, not a source rebuild.
- **ARCH-11-FR-087** — Mutable convenience tags such as `latest` MAY exist, but deployments/releases SHALL be traceable to immutable SHA tags/digests.
- **ARCH-11-FR-088** — PRs from untrusted forks SHALL not receive package-write credentials.
- **ARCH-11-FR-089** — Registry/package permissions SHALL use least privilege.

### Test evidence and traceability

- **ARCH-11-FR-090** — CI SHALL upload machine-readable test result summaries where practical.
- **ARCH-11-FR-091** — Test names, metadata or traceability manifests SHALL reference PRD/ARCH acceptance/test IDs for implementation-ticket traceability.
- **ARCH-11-FR-092** — Pull requests SHOULD include or link to the successful CI run and relevant executed test evidence before associated PRD tickets are closed.
- **ARCH-11-FR-093** — Build/release metadata SHALL make it possible to determine which PRD implementation commit produced any running image.

## 9. Detailed interaction behaviour

### Pull request

1. Check out the exact PR commit.
2. Calculate build metadata.
3. Run web, .NET and PostgreSQL/pgvector quality suites in parallel where possible.
4. Require `source-quality-gate`.
5. Build web/API/Worker images once.
6. Export immutable image artifacts.
7. Load those artifacts into the integration environment.
8. Run Compose/container integration.
9. Run Playwright/other E2E against that same stack.
10. Scan those same images and generate SBOMs.
11. Require final `required-ci`.
12. Generate a short-retention downloadable release-candidate bundle.

### Default branch

Perform all PR checks plus:

- produce longer-retention release bundle;
- optionally publish exact images to GHCR;
- generate provenance/attestation where enabled.

### Version tag/release

Perform the full pipeline with release-version metadata and publish only after `required-ci` succeeds.

### Failure behaviour

- No mandatory-check failure may still produce a successful release/publish state.
- Diagnostic artifacts/logs should remain available when practical.
- A test retry may be used only for explicitly identified flaky infrastructure failures; product test failures must not be automatically hidden by repeated retry-until-pass behaviour.
- Any security exception must be explicit, documented and time-bounded rather than silently ignored.

## 10. Business / architecture rules

- **Build once, test once, promote the exact artifact.**
- CI validates the deployable system, not a parallel development-only runtime.
- Organization/tenant and Owner Portal security boundaries are mandatory CI concerns.
- PostgreSQL+RLS integration testing is mandatory before release.
- Application containers are immutable; environment configuration is external.
- CI artifacts never contain production secrets.
- A source commit is not considered releasable merely because unit tests pass.
- Main/tag publication must not bypass the same core runtime/security gates used for PR release candidates.
- New deployable services/datastores/brokers require an architecture decision and corresponding CI coverage.

## 11. Permission rules

GitHub workflow permissions must follow least privilege.

At minimum:

- test jobs: read-only repository permissions wherever possible;
- package publication: `packages: write` only in the trusted publish job;
- artifact attestations: only the specific attestation permissions required by GitHub when enabled;
- no production environment secrets in PR jobs;
- no privileged token execution of untrusted fork code;
- environment approvals may be added for actual deployment, which remains outside this PRD.

Application test identities must have only the privileges required for each scenario. Cross-tenant and portal-boundary tests must exercise realistic restricted identities.

## 12. Data requirements

CI test data must be deterministic, synthetic and safe to persist in workflow artifacts.

Database integration fixtures must include:

- at least two Organizations/tenants;
- authorized and unauthorized users;
- representative internal and portal identities when implemented;
- records sufficient to test RLS and confidentiality;
- vector records when pgvector features are implemented.

No production personal information or production database dump is permitted in ordinary CI.

## 13. API requirements

CI shall exercise stable operational endpoints such as:

- API liveness/health;
- API readiness where separate;
- runtime/build metadata;
- Worker heartbeat/readiness or equivalent.

Application-level API tests must verify stable error contracts and non-disclosing authorization failures.

The external web-container smoke check must verify that Nginx/proxy routing reaches the API health endpoint through the same route expected in production.

## 14. Real-time / event requirements

When SignalR/realtime is implemented, CI must verify:

- initial connection;
- authorized subscription;
- representative event delivery;
- disconnect/reconnect;
- tenant-safe event isolation.

Worker/outbox integration tests must verify:

- persisted outbox/job record;
- worker acquisition;
- tenant context;
- successful processing;
- retry/idempotency;
- failure/dead-letter state;
- resulting domain/audit event.

## 15. UX requirements

Browser E2E must exercise the compiled production SPA served by the web container.

On test failure, CI should retain Playwright trace/screenshot/video evidence sufficient to reproduce UI failures.

The application should expose build metadata in a support-accessible location so operators can match UI/API/Worker versions to the CI run.

## 16. Accessibility requirements

CI must include automated accessibility checks for critical MUI-based user flows where practical, and component/E2E tests must cover keyboard-critical interactions such as dialogs, forms and Kanban movement.

Automated checks do not replace manual WCAG review, but regressions detectable by automation should fail the relevant CI gate.

## 17. Error and empty states

CI must fail with explicit diagnostics for:

- missing lock files/dependencies;
- compile/type/lint failure;
- migration failure;
- PostgreSQL/pgvector unavailable;
- RLS/tenant isolation failure;
- API/Worker failed startup;
- unhealthy Compose service;
- web reverse-proxy failure;
- E2E failure;
- vulnerability policy violation;
- secret scan failure;
- incomplete/corrupt release bundle.

Errors and uploaded logs must not disclose repository secrets, passwords, connection credentials or sensitive test values.

## 18. Edge cases

The CI design must cover or explicitly account for:

- cancelled/superseded PR runs;
- forks with no secrets;
- duplicate workflow execution;
- cache miss/corruption;
- container build interruption;
- database startup delay;
- migration race;
- Worker restart during a pending job;
- API restart during browser session;
- stale/mismatched web/API/Worker build IDs;
- tag build from an unverified commit;
- registry outage after successful testing;
- artifact upload failure;
- security scanner outage versus actual vulnerability result;
- previous schema unavailable for upgrade test;
- generated SBOM/checksum mismatch.

## 19. Non-functional requirements

- Reproducibility
- Deterministic dependency installation
- Least privilege
- Secret isolation
- Artifact immutability
- Build/release provenance
- Fast parallel feedback where safe
- Fail-closed required gates
- Traceability to source commit
- Actionable diagnostics
- Reasonable PR runtime target with heavier/nightly suites separated only when explicitly approved
- No dependence on a developer workstation

Initial CI performance target:

- fast source-quality feedback should begin immediately and run in parallel;
- ordinary PR required CI should target completion within approximately 15–20 minutes as the codebase matures, without weakening mandatory security/integration coverage;
- longer exhaustive/nightly tests may supplement but not replace critical PR gates.

## 20. Analytics / telemetry

Capture/retain as appropriate:

- total CI duration;
- per-job duration;
- pass/fail/cancelled state;
- test counts/failures;
- flaky-test retry counts if retries are explicitly allowed;
- container build duration/cache hit rate;
- image sizes;
- vulnerability counts by severity;
- artifact sizes;
- release-bundle SHA/digest metadata.

CI metrics must not expose secrets or production data.

## 21. Dependencies

- **ARCH-01** Repository, Solution and Technology Baseline
- **ARCH-03** ASP.NET Core Modular-Monolith API Architecture
- **ARCH-04** PostgreSQL Persistence, Tenant Isolation and Schema Evolution
- **ARCH-07** Integrations, AI, Email and Background Processing Architecture
- **ARCH-08** Observability, Health, Audit and Operational Resilience
- **ARCH-09** Automated Test Architecture and Engineering Quality Gates
- **ARCH-10** Docker Images, Compose Runtime and Local/Hosted Execution
- **ARCH-12** Configuration, Secrets, Environments, Promotion and Rollback

## 22. Out of scope

- automatic deployment to a particular cloud/provider;
- mandatory Kubernetes;
- production database migration execution policy beyond what is required to test/release the images;
- full CD/environment promotion workflow;
- mandatory RabbitMQ/Kafka/Redis;
- rebuilding release images on the target host.

## 23. Acceptance criteria

- **ARCH-11-AC-001** — GIVEN a PR commit WHEN CI runs THEN web-quality, dotnet-quality and PostgreSQL/pgvector integration checks execute and a mandatory failure prevents the source-quality gate.
- **ARCH-11-AC-002** — GIVEN a tenant-isolation/RLS regression WHEN the PostgreSQL integration suite executes THEN CI fails.
- **ARCH-11-AC-003** — GIVEN a clean PostgreSQL+pgvector database WHEN migrations run THEN the current schema is created successfully and the API can start against it.
- **ARCH-11-AC-004** — GIVEN a green source-quality gate WHEN application images are built THEN exactly web/API/Worker release-candidate images are produced from the same commit.
- **ARCH-11-AC-005** — GIVEN the built images WHEN downstream integration/E2E/security jobs execute THEN they load and test the exact image artifacts rather than rebuilding source.
- **ARCH-11-AC-006** — GIVEN `compose.release.yml` WHEN inspected THEN web/API/Worker use `image:` references and contain no app `build:` directives.
- **ARCH-11-AC-007** — GIVEN the exact containerized stack WHEN health smoke tests run THEN web serving, web->API proxying, API readiness and Worker processing/heartbeat succeed.
- **ARCH-11-AC-008** — GIVEN an Owner Portal/internal authorization test WHEN a portal identity requests an internal protected resource THEN the request is denied without protected data leakage.
- **ARCH-11-AC-009** — GIVEN an image with a vulnerability violating the configured blocking policy WHEN security scanning runs THEN `required-ci` fails and release/publish is blocked.
- **ARCH-11-AC-010** — GIVEN a mandatory E2E or container-integration failure WHEN CI completes THEN `required-ci` fails.
- **ARCH-11-AC-011** — GIVEN a successful `required-ci` WHEN the release bundle is generated THEN it contains the exact tested web/API/Worker images, Compose file, env example, checksums, build metadata, SBOMs and run instructions.
- **ARCH-11-AC-012** — GIVEN the downloaded bundle on a clean Docker host WHEN images are loaded and documented environment values supplied THEN StrataAI2 starts without source, Node or .NET SDK.
- **ARCH-11-AC-013** — GIVEN any released image WHEN its metadata is inspected THEN the originating repository, commit SHA/build ID and application version are identifiable.
- **ARCH-11-AC-014** — GIVEN a pull request from an untrusted fork WHEN CI executes THEN privileged registry/project/production secrets are not exposed to the PR code.
- **ARCH-11-AC-015** — GIVEN a successful trusted main/tag run WHEN images are published to GHCR THEN the published digests correspond to the same artifacts that passed `required-ci`, with no source rebuild.
- **ARCH-11-AC-016** — GIVEN the release bundle WHEN SHA-256 verification runs THEN every listed artifact matches `SHA256SUMS`.
- **ARCH-11-AC-017** — GIVEN a failed browser E2E test WHEN CI completes THEN diagnostic trace/screenshot evidence is retained according to artifact policy.
- **ARCH-11-AC-018** — GIVEN a Worker job that is retried/replayed in integration testing WHEN processing completes THEN idempotency rules prevent duplicate material side effects.
- **ARCH-11-AC-019** — GIVEN a SignalR/realtime feature is present WHEN its required CI test runs THEN an authorized client receives permitted events and an unauthorized/cross-tenant client does not.
- **ARCH-11-AC-020** — GIVEN branch protection is configured WHEN a required underlying CI dependency fails/skips/cancels THEN the stable aggregate `required-ci` check cannot report success.

## 24. Test scenarios

- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-01** — Web typecheck/lint/unit/component/build pass on valid source.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-02** — Intentional TypeScript/type failure causes required CI failure.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-03** — .NET build/test failure causes required CI failure.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-04** — PostgreSQL clean-schema migration succeeds.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-05** — Previous supported schema upgrades successfully.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-06** — PostgreSQL RLS blocks cross-Organization read.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-07** — PostgreSQL RLS blocks cross-Organization write.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-08** — Missing tenant context fails closed.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-09** — pgvector extension and representative vector query work.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-10** — Web/API/Worker images are built once and exported.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-11** — Downstream job loads exact exported image artifacts.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-12** — Container stack boots PostgreSQL, object storage, API, Worker and web.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-13** — API health/readiness succeeds.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-14** — Worker executes a representative queued/outbox job.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-15** — Web root serves compiled SPA.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-16** — Web `/api/health` reverse-proxy path succeeds.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-17** — Representative authenticated Playwright flow succeeds.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-18** — Owner Portal identity is denied internal-only API/resource.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-19** — Kanban keyboard drag/drop persists correctly when feature exists.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-20** — SignalR authorized event/reconnect path passes when feature exists.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-21** — Cross-tenant realtime subscription is rejected/filtered when feature exists.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-22** — Worker duplicate/retry test proves material idempotency.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-23** — Node dependency vulnerability scan executes.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-24** — .NET dependency vulnerability scan executes.
- [ ] **ARCH-11-TC-25** — Secret-detection scan executes and fails on seeded forbidden secret fixture/test.

## 25. Definition of done

ARCH-11 is complete only when:

- GitHub Actions implements all required jobs/gates;
- web/API/Worker are built once per release candidate;
- the exact built artifacts are used by all downstream integration/security/release jobs;
- PostgreSQL 17+ with pgvector integration tests pass;
- Organization/RLS isolation tests pass;
- API, Worker and web Compose smoke tests pass;
- Playwright E2E runs against the actual containerized candidate;
- supply-chain/dependency/secret/image security checks are active;
- SBOMs are generated for all application images;
- the stable final `required-ci` check accurately reflects mandatory dependencies;
- branch protection can require that stable check;
- CI produces a downloadable no-rebuild Docker release bundle;
- the release bundle has been independently validated on a clean Docker environment;
- main/tag registry publication, if enabled, promotes the same tested image digest;
- CI/documentation explains local reproduction and failure diagnosis;
- no unresolved P0/P1 CI/security defects remain.

## 26. Open questions

- Confirm exact GitHub Actions artifact retention values; recommended defaults are 14 days for PR candidates and 90 days for main/tag artifacts.
- Confirm whether main builds immediately publish to GHCR or only version-tag/release builds do.
- Select the specific security scanners/SBOM tooling (e.g. Trivy/Grype, Syft, Gitleaks) while preserving this PRD's required outcomes.
- Decide whether GitHub artifact attestations are enabled immediately or after the repository/package publication workflow is established.
- Define which exhaustive suites, if any, move to nightly CI; critical tenant/security/container/E2E gates must remain on PRs.
- Define the previous-schema fixture strategy once the first production schema version is established.

## Agent execution contract

- Treat this PRD as the authoritative CI/release architecture for StrataAI2.
- Implement CI incrementally as the codebase is scaffolded, but do not weaken the final required gates.
- Build the three application images exactly once and pass those image artifacts downstream.
- Do not replace PostgreSQL/RLS integration tests with mocks.
- Do not expose privileged secrets to untrusted PR execution.
- Do not rebuild application images in release or registry-publish jobs.
- Add/maintain test traceability using ARCH/PRD acceptance/test IDs.
- Link implementation PRs to this issue and include CI/test evidence.
- Any deliberate exception to a mandatory security/release gate requires a documented architecture decision.
